_comment: The third sentence: timing. Seven transiting bodies, two states each.
Index 0 is applying (still tightening towards exact), index 1 is
The two entries per body differ in TIMESCALE rather than in flavour,
because that is the genuinely body-specific part: the Moon finishes an
aspect in hours and Saturn takes months. They deliberately carry none of
the transiting planet's character. An earlier version did, and a Mercury
clause about things being said kept landing under a Venus headline about
making a room nicer, which read as two sentences from different pages.

moon: This is still tightening, and it peaks later today.
It passed exact earlier today and is already letting go.
sun: It is still closing, so tomorrow is more of this rather than less.
The exact point is a day or two behind you now.
mercury: It is still closing, and it holds for another day or so.
It has passed exact; what is left of it goes quickly.
venus: Still tightening. It has a couple of days left to run.
Past exact now, and fading over the next few days.
mars: Still building. This one has the better part of a week in it.
It broke a few days ago. The rest is aftermath.
jupiter: Still closing, and slowly: this one is measured in weeks.
Past its closest point, and it will take weeks to clear.
saturn: Still tightening, and it will be months before it is done.
It has turned the corner, though it will lift only gradually.
